meta.description: Assumptions register and default values. Every input the engine reads is listed here with its value, its status, its source and the reason it was chosen. The page builds its input panel from this file.

statusVocabulary.statutory: Set by an Indian statute or rule and cited.
statusVocabulary.secondary: Taken from a secondary source that cites primary documents; must be checked against the primary source.
statusVocabulary.placeholder: No authoritative source exists; a stand-in value so the calculator runs. Replace with your own figure.
statusVocabulary.illustrative: Invented for illustration in the design discussion. Not a finding. Replace with your own figure.
statusVocabulary.user: A choice only the user can make; the default is neutral.
statusVocabulary.constant: A unit conversion or arithmetic constant.

assumptions.label: Patients per month
assumptions.reason: The main control. All routes are plotted against it.

assumptions.label: Pages per patient
assumptions.reason: Synthetic workload from the design discussion.

assumptions.label: Input tokens per page
assumptions.reason: Synthetic: 18,000 input tokens over 12 pages. Image inputs can cost far more tokens per page; measure on your own scans.

assumptions.label: Output tokens per page
assumptions.reason: Synthetic: 4,800 output tokens over 12 pages. Reasoning models can multiply this.

assumptions.label: Measured input tokens per patient (overrides the above)
assumptions.reason: Preferred over the page-based estimate: take the average from a sample of real extraction runs.

assumptions.label: Measured output tokens per patient (overrides the above)
assumptions.reason: As above.

assumptions.label: Exchange rate
assumptions.reason: API and hyperscaler prices are quoted in US dollars. Set today's rate.

assumptions.label: GST on cloud bills (not recoverable)
assumptions.reason: Cloud services are taxed at 18%. Hospital healthcare services are exempt, so input tax credit is generally unavailable and the tax is a real cost. A hospital with taxable supplies (pharmacy, rooms above the threshold) may recover part of it by apportionment under section 17 and Rule 42. Set lower on your tax adviser's advice.

assumptions.label: API price, input
assumptions.reason: Invented price for a small extraction model. Copy the real figure from the vendor's price page and record the date.

assumptions.label: API price, output
assumptions.reason: As above.

assumptions.label: API processes data inside India
assumptions.reason: Used only by the data-residency rule.

assumptions.label: Rented GPU tier
assumptions.reason: Three tiers to normalise against: subsidised government, Indian commercial, hyperscaler. The default stays at the brief's government rate, but portal access requires eligibility (researchers, startups and MSMEs, students, government entities) that most private hospitals lack; see open item OI-11, which is left to the author.

assumptions.label: Your own GPU-hour price (for 'Your own quote')
assumptions.reason: Used only when the tier is set to your own quote.

assumptions.label: Patients processed per rented GPU-hour
assumptions.reason: Throughput is model, GPU and batching specific. The rented tiers are H100-class while the owned default is an older rig, so the two throughputs differ; measure both, or fill in the token speeds below.

assumptions.label: Rented GPU: input tokens per second (optional)
assumptions.reason: If both speeds are given, throughput is derived as 3600 / (input tokens / input speed + output tokens / output speed).

assumptions.label: Rented GPU: output tokens per second (optional)
assumptions.reason: As above.

assumptions.label: Share of billed GPU-hours doing useful work
assumptions.reason: 1 assumes perfect packing, which flatters renting. Hourly billing, start-up time and idle reservations lower it.

assumptions.label: Rig purchase price, including GST
assumptions.reason: Illustrative two-GPU previous-generation server. The calculator deliberately does not assume top-end hardware. Use a vendor quote.

assumptions.label: GPUs in the rig
assumptions.reason: Capacity scales with GPU count.

assumptions.label: Patients processed per owned GPU-hour
assumptions.reason: Older GPUs are slower per hour but can be ample for small extraction models. Measure it.

assumptions.label: Owned GPU: input tokens per second (optional)
assumptions.reason: Derives throughput as for the rented GPU.

assumptions.label: Owned GPU: output tokens per second (optional)
assumptions.reason: As above.

assumptions.label: Effective hardware life
assumptions.reason: Schedule II, Part C item XII(i), gives servers and networks a 6-year useful life (3 years is for end-user devices); bare text read in full. A GPU rig is a server. This is an accounting life, not a forecast of obsolescence: set 3 to match the brief or a faster refresh, or longer for older GPUs used for small models. Schedule II binds companies; trust, society and government hospitals may use other conventions.

history.reason: Brief cited 3 years for computers; Schedule II Part C item XII(i) gives 6 years for servers and networks, which is the class a GPU server belongs to.

assumptions.verification: bare text read on a secondary host (AdvocateKhoj), not the MCA gazette

assumptions.label: Residual value at end of life
assumptions.reason: Your choice. Schedule II ordinarily caps residual value at 5% of original cost; zero is the cautious default.

assumptions.label: Tax depreciation rate (written-down value)
assumptions.reason: Computers including software: 40% WDV, retained under the Income-tax Act, 2025. Shown for information only; it is a tax view, not the monthly cost. Irrelevant to a tax-exempt charitable hospital.

assumptions.label: Cost of money (annual interest rate)
assumptions.reason: Zero means straight-line depreciation with no interest, which flatters buying. Enter your borrowing rate; the output lists it as not included while it is zero.

assumptions.label: Annual GPU failure rate
assumptions.reason: (148 faulty-GPU + 72 HBM3 interruptions) / 16,384 GPUs x 365/54 days = 0.091. One operator, a training workload, a 54-day window annualised, and interruptions rather than replacements. Not an Indian or inference figure.
assumptions.verification: section 3.3.4 read via a fetch tool (partial page)

assumptions.label: Share of rig price that is GPUs
assumptions.reason: A failed GPU costs a GPU, not a whole rig. Take it from your quote.

assumptions.label: Share of failures not covered by warranty
assumptions.reason: 1 is cautious. Lower it for the warranty period.

assumptions.label: Share of hours the rig is available for this work
assumptions.reason: Allows for maintenance, downtime and other workloads. Sets capacity only.

assumptions.label: Hours per month
assumptions.reason: 8,760 hours a year / 12.

assumptions.label: Maintenance and support contract
assumptions.reason: Use your annual maintenance contract divided by 12.

assumptions.label: Land and building, amortised
assumptions.reason: Deliberately not computed: pooled estates, existing parcels and new purchases differ too much. Leave blank and every output says land is not included.

assumptions.label: State (grid electricity)
assumptions.reason: Commercial or HT landed tariff from the state table. Domestic rates are not offered.

assumptions.label: Your own grid tariff (overrides the table)
assumptions.reason: Use your last bill: total charges divided by units, including demand charges, duty and surcharges.

assumptions.label: Use captive or open-access solar instead
assumptions.reason: Replaces the grid tariff with the landed cost below.

assumptions.label: Solar PPA rate
assumptions.reason: Headline PPA rates are about 3 to 4 rupees, but regulated charges can more than double the landed cost.

assumptions.label: Wheeling and transmission charges
assumptions.reason: From the state open-access order.

assumptions.label: Cross-subsidy and additional surcharge
assumptions.reason: Captive users may be exempt from some surcharges; check the order.

assumptions.label: Other charges (banking, duty, scheduling)
assumptions.reason: Any remaining per-unit charge.

assumptions.label: Transmission and distribution losses
assumptions.reason: Landed cost is grossed up for units lost before delivery.

assumptions.label: Rig power draw at full load
assumptions.reason: Measure at the wall, or use the vendor's figure.

assumptions.label: Idle draw as a share of full load
assumptions.reason: A switched-on rig draws power while idle. The brief's formula assumed zero.

assumptions.label: Cooling overhead (PUE)
assumptions.reason: Total facility power divided by IT power. A hospital server room in a hot climate may be well above a data centre's.

assumptions.label: One-time build and integration
assumptions.reason: Invented in the design discussion.

assumptions.label: Months to spread the build cost over
assumptions.reason: Choose the period you expect the system to run before a rebuild.

assumptions.label: Recurring engineering support
assumptions.reason: Maintenance, drift checks and fixes.

assumptions.label: How the review fraction is set

options.label: Work it out from the accuracy I need

assumptions.reason: Links required accuracy to review effort.

assumptions.label: Share of outputs reviewed by staff
assumptions.reason: The most sensitive input. Measure it in a pilot.

assumptions.label: Required accuracy after review
assumptions.reason: Used when the review fraction is worked out from accuracy.

assumptions.label: Records with at least one model error, before review
assumptions.reason: Comes from your validation study, not from vendor claims.

assumptions.label: Share of errors a reviewer catches
assumptions.reason: Reviewers miss errors too.

assumptions.label: Targeting factor (1 = random review)
assumptions.reason: If review is aimed at low-confidence outputs, errors are concentrated in the reviewed set. 2 means the reviewed set holds twice its share of errors.

assumptions.label: Minutes per review
assumptions.reason: Time it in a pilot.

assumptions.label: Reviewer cost per minute
assumptions.reason: Monthly cost to employer divided by working minutes.

assumptions.label: Initial validation sample
assumptions.reason: Size it with a statistician for the accuracy you need to demonstrate.

assumptions.label: Clinician minutes per record
assumptions.reason: Time to build or check the reference answer.

assumptions.label: Analysis and report
assumptions.reason: Statistics, write-up and sign-off.

assumptions.label: Governance: ethics committee, DPDP Act compliance, CDSCO clearance if the tool is a medical device
assumptions.reason: One-time. Under the DPDP Act 2023 a formal impact assessment is required only of Significant Data Fiduciaries. Spread over the same months as the validation study; the brief listed these costs but left them out of the total.

assumptions.label: Months to spread validation and governance over
Changes a year that need re-validation
assumptions.reason: New model version, report template, scanner or printer format, or language.

assumptions.label: Cost per reference answer (blank = same as initial study)
assumptions.reason: Defaults to clinician plus annotator cost per record.

assumptions.label: Share of outputs audited each month
assumptions.reason: Random audit to measure drift, separate from operational review. If the same staff do both, avoid counting them twice.

assumptions.label: Cost per uncaught error (scenario)
assumptions.reason: No authoritative figure exists. Leave blank and the output lists error cost as not included.

assumptions.label: Minutes of manual entry per patient
assumptions.reason: The brief's 20 rupees per patient, split as 4 minutes at 5 rupees. A pure guess: time it.

assumptions.label: Manual cost per patient (overrides the two above)
Records with a manual-entry error
assumptions.reason: Manual entry makes errors too. Counted only when the cost per uncaught error is also set, so the comparison is like for like.

assumptions.label: Data-residency rule

options.label: Data may not leave the hospital

assumptions.reason: A policy constraint, not a cost: it removes routes rather than pricing them.

assumptions.label: What if cloud prices change? Repricing factor (scenario)
assumptions.reason: Tests what happens if investor-subsidised or promotional prices end. A scenario, not a forecast; no public evidence yet supports a default.

assumptions.label: Share paid by the hospital
assumptions.reason: In out-of-pocket care the hospital's cost often reaches patients through package prices; set the patient share to reflect that if it applies.

assumptions.label: Share paid by insurer or government scheme
Share paid by a pooled consortium
Centres sharing one validated system
assumptions.reason: 1 means no pooling.

assumptions.label: Patients per month at each centre
Share of validation each centre must still do locally
assumptions.reason: Accuracy must be shown on each hospital's own documents, so pooling cannot share all of validation.

alwaysExcluded: Downtime and fallback to manual entry
Scanning paper into images, if not already digital
Model or software licence fees beyond the API price
